title: Refrigerator Compartment Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The fridge (R) compartment thermistor is out of range.
fullDescription:
H01 on Panasonic Econavi refrigerators indicates the refrigerator compartment thermistor has failed. The inverter compressor cannot modulate cooling based on accurate temperature.

Replace the sensor to restore Econavi optimization.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access top-rear of fridge liner and swap thermistor.

title: Freezer Compartment Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The freezer (F) compartment thermistor is faulty.
fullDescription:
H02 indicates the freezer thermistor is open, shorted, or out of range. Freezer temperature regulation fails.

Replace sensor; often paired with H01 replacement kit.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Access freezer liner and swap thermistor.

title: Evaporator Sensor Fault
fullDescription:
H03 indicates the evaporator coil sensor is out of range. Defrost cycles rely on this input; without it, frost accumulates.

Replace sensor promptly to prevent freezer fan blockage.

fixSteps.title: Empty freezer
fixSteps.instruction: Move frozen items to a cooler.

title: Defrost Heater Fault
shortDescription: Defrost heater circuit not drawing current.
fullDescription:
H04 indicates the defrost heater element is open or the bimetal thermostat has failed. Ice will build up on the evaporator, reducing cooling.

Test heater and thermostat continuity and replace as required.

fixSteps.title: Replace parts
fixSteps.instruction: Install new defrost heater or bimetal.

title: Ambient / Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Econavi ambient or humidity sensor is faulty.
fullDescription:
H05 indicates Econavi's ambient temperature/humidity sensor has failed. The adaptive energy-saving features cannot function, though basic cooling still runs.

Replace the Econavi sensor module.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Swap Econavi sensor module near control area.

whenToCallPro: If you can't locate the sensor.

faq.a: Yes; only energy savings are affected.

title: Inverter Compressor Fault
shortDescription: Communication or drive fault with the inverter compressor.
fullDescription:
H06 indicates the inverter driver cannot control the compressor - either no current, overcurrent, or loss of rotor-position feedback.

This is a serious fault and typically requires inverter board or compressor replacement.

fixSteps.title: Service call
fixSteps.instruction: Technician needed for inverter diagnosis and replacement.

faq.a: Depends on age; sometimes a new fridge is comparable in cost.

title: Freezer Fan Fault
fullDescription:
H07 indicates the freezer fan motor is not spinning at commanded speed. Blocked blade or failed motor are typical causes.

Check for icing first.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If H07 persists, replace DC fan motor.

whenToCallPro: If repetitive icing indicates deeper issue.

faq.a: Ensure door seals well and defrost system is healthy.

title: Damper Motor Fault
shortDescription: Air damper between fridge and freezer is stuck.
fullDescription:
H08 indicates the damper motor that controls cold-air flow between freezer and fridge is not reporting correct position. Cold air distribution will be incorrect.

Replace the damper assembly.
symptoms: Fridge too cold or too warm

fixSteps.title: Access damper
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear fridge panel or top shelf housing.

faq.a: Possibly if damper stuck open in fridge.

title: Ice Maker Fault
fullDescription:
H09 indicates the ice maker module has failed or is disconnected. The rest of the fridge operates normally.

Check ice maker harness; replace module if needed.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and reseat ice maker connector.

faq.a: H09 is mechanical; water issues produce different symptoms.

title: Door Switch Fault
fullDescription:
H10 indicates the door switch has been on or open for abnormally long. Causes: misaligned door, stuck switch, or a misaligned door alarm.

Check door alignment and switch action.

fixSteps.title: Align door
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust hinges if door sits low.

faq.a: Yes, but alarm is annoying and interior light behaves oddly.

title: Power Supply Fault
shortDescription: Main board detected abnormal supply voltage.
fullDescription:
H11 indicates the main control has seen supply voltage outside acceptable range. Common during brownouts or when used with inverter/generator power.

Verify a clean, dedicated circuit.

title: Communication Fault
shortDescription: Main board and display not communicating.
fullDescription:
H12 indicates loss of serial communication between main PCB and the user interface. Cooling continues in fail-safe mode.

Reseat harnesses first.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harnesses
fixSteps.instruction: Open control housing and reseat ribbon.

fixSteps.title: Replace UI board
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, swap the UI module.
